differences: Recordings of one subject number (6 recordings, three visits) have no row in TCPCHA_Subjects.csv, so group, age and sex are empty for that participant, while the table has one subject number that has no recordings (a Control participant). They may be the same person with a mistyped number, but this was not assumed and the two were not merged; 87 participants have recordings. The 60 Tai Chi-naive and 27 expert participants counted in the checks are those of the subjects table. The design paper (2013) describes the planned trial: 60 Tai Chi-naive adults, 30 per arm. The deposit holds 29 control and 31 Tai Chi participants at the first visit (60 in total); 27 experts are in the data but not in the design paper. The PhysioNet entry (version 1.0.2, Dec 2021) is the data release, titled 'Tai Chi, Physiological Complexity, and Healthy Aging - Gait'; the design paper is the one the curator listed as the original publication.
